channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77642-6

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is clinically heterogeneous, complicating efforts to identify patients at highest risk. Here, the authors show that integrating proteomics with machine learning reveals two biologically distinct subtypes with different prognoses, including a high-risk inflammatory cardiorenal phenotype.
item.dc:title: Multimodal data-driven clustering analysis of heart failure patients identifies two distinct patterns of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: Results from the PACIFIC-PRESERVED study

item.title: Compound Z247611722 Exhibits Antifungal Activity by Inhibiting Serine Palmitoyltransferase
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77817-1

This study identifies and characterizes Z247611722, a novel fungicidal compound active against multiple Candida species, and demonstrates that it inhibits sphingolipid biosynthesis by targeting serine palmitoyltransferase.
item.dc:title: Compound Z247611722 Exhibits Antifungal Activity by Inhibiting Serine Palmitoyltransferase

item.title: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77619-5

Here the authors develop an AI framework called E-MAF that, starting from a desired release profile, couples process-aware prediction with expert-mimic evolutionary search to generate interpretable, lab-ready formulations for controlled release systems.
item.dc:title: On-demand design of controlled-release systems using an expert-mimic AI framework

item.title: Loss of NCOA6 protein causes aggressive prostate cancer with EGFR overexpression and dependency
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77701-y

EGFR is frequently overexpressed in prostate cancer. Here, the authors show that the transcriptional co-activator NCOA6 and the nuclear transcription factor NFY form a regulatory complex that restricts EGFR overexpression and suppresses prostate cancer development.
item.dc:title: Loss of NCOA6 protein causes aggressive prostate cancer with EGFR overexpression and dependency

item.title: Near-Zero Creep Ionic Elastomer for Non-drifting Ear Electroencephalogram Signal Acquisition
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77777-6

Polymer electrodes are promising for wearable ear electroencephalogram sensors, though they are sensitive to polymer creep under sustained strain. Here the authors report a crosslinked copolymer which resists creep for stable sensing.
item.dc:title: Near-Zero Creep Ionic Elastomer for Non-drifting Ear Electroencephalogram Signal Acquisition

item.title: Biofilm formation and dynamics in the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77598-7

In this study, the authors show that Prochlorococcus picocyanobacteria form biofilms and dynamically transition between free-living and attached states with significantly different physiology, thus suggesting a role for these bacteria in deep-ocean carbon export.
item.dc:title: Biofilm formation and dynamics in the marine cyanobacterium Prochlorococcus

item.title: Fully integrated quantum frequency processor on a silicon chip
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77287-5

Frequency-bin encoding offers high-dimensional quantum information processing, but scalable deployment requires miniaturization. Here, the authors demonstrate quantum state generation and coherent manipulation on a CMOS-compatible photonic processor.
item.dc:title: Fully integrated quantum frequency processor on a silicon chip

item.title: Optical beam shaping induced reconfigurable magnetic domains
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77572-3

All-optical switching of the magnetic state offers the potential for ultrafast writing of information in the form of magnetic bits. While it has been implemented in simple and technologically relevant magnetic stacks, these have hitherto required helicity control. Here, Khalid and coauthors demonstrate how optical tailoring can overcome helicity constraints in /Pt/Co stacks.
item.dc:title: Optical beam shaping induced reconfigurable magnetic domains
